conventions.valueAsPublished: The value exactly as the 'Internal coordinates' table of the CCCBDB page prints it, digits and trailing zeros included (pages re-fetched 2026-10-03). null where the page prints no row for the value: the three PCl5 angles, which rest on the stated point group.
conventions.fixedBySymmetry: true where the molecule's point group, as the CCCBDB page states it, fixes the angle whatever the bond lengths are: CO2 (D∞h), CH4 (Td), BF3 (D3h), SF6 (Oh), XeF4 (D4h) and PCl5 (D3h). The build stores the point group beside such an angle, and the card says that the symmetry fixes it. Set for CO2 on 2026-10-04: a D∞h molecule is linear, so its 180 is fixed in the same way as the 180 of SF6.
conventions.origin: Central atom at the origin where there is one (H2O, CO2, NH3, CH4, BF3, SO2, SF6, XeF4, PCl5); centre of mass at the origin for O2, N2, HCl, H2O2. Each molecule's 'origin' field states its own.
conventions.bonds: 'atoms' is one representative pair; 'appliesTo' lists every symmetry-equivalent pair with that cited length. Same for angles ([end, centre, end]).
conventions.lengthType: re = equilibrium, r0 = vibrational ground state, null = source does not say
conventions.pubchemCid: Each CID was confirmed on 2026-10-03 by CAS lookup at https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/name/<CAS>/property/MolecularFormula,IUPACName,Title/CSV Re-confirmed by the verifier on 2026-10-03 with the same lookup for all 13.
conventions.bondOrder: bondList.order is authored structure (spec 5.1 exempt field), not a cited value
conventions.source: All 13 molecules use the NIST CCCBDB experimental-geometry table value (printed precision) as the cited value.

verification.method: Independent pass. All 13 CCCBDB experimental-geometry pages were re-fetched with curl (not reused from raw/), parsed, and compared to the file by script; geometry was recomputed from the stored coordinates with a separate script (verify-geometry/verify.py), not build_geometry.py.

scriptChecks.tolerances: 0.001 A, 0.1 degree; 0.002 A against CCCBDB's own 4-decimal Cartesians

checked: Every cited bond length, angle and the H2O2 dihedral equals the table value on the freshly fetched CCCBDB page for that CAS number (13 molecules; PCl5 has length rows only).
Every CCCBDB reference squib and comment quoted in the citations (re / r0 / 'symmetry' / axial / equatorial, author, journal, pages, DOI) was read on the fetched page.

Point groups against the CCCBDB page (12 agree; H2O2 is printed C2h there and recorded C2 here, which the stored coordinates satisfy: the map (x,y,z)->(x,-y,-z) exchanges the two OH halves and there is no mirror plane or inversion centre).

Coordinates reproduce every cited length and angle on every symmetry-equivalent index set; bondList equals the union of appliesTo; every bond angle about every multi-coordinate atom is listed exactly once; centre-of-mass or central-atom origin as stated; spec 5.1 rule 3 minimum bond lengths.
All interatomic distances against CCCBDB's own Cartesian table (max difference 0.0007 A, NH3).
CAS check digits (all 13 valid) and PubChem CID by CAS lookup at PubChem PUG REST (all 13 match; formulas match).
Authored bond orders: formal charges are all zero with standard lone pairs, and Pauling oxidation states sum to zero (H2O2 O is -1, SO2 S is +4, XeF4 Xe is +4, PCl5 P is +5, SF6 S is +6).

Second independent source, diatomics: NIST Chemistry WebBook 'Constants of diatomic molecules' (Huber and Herzberg) ground-state re: O2 1.20752 (https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7782447&Units=SI&Mask=1000), N2 1.097685 (ID=C7727379), HCl 1.274552 (ID=C7647010). These round to the file's 1.208, 1.098, 1.275.
Second independent source, H2O2: abstract of Redington, Olson, Cross 1962 at https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1063/1.1732733 states OO 1.475, OH 0.950, dihedral 119.8, OOH 94.8.
Second independent source, XeF4: abstract of Buerger et al. 1996 at https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1063/1.471266 states r0 = 193.487(3) pm.

flagsForOwner: The cited values mix structure types: re for H2O, CH4, O2, N2, HCl, BF3; r0 for XeF4; unlabelled on CCCBDB for CO2, NH3, SO2, SF6, PCl5, H2O2. Differences between types are a few thousandths of an angstrom, far inside the spec's 0.01 A / 1 degree acceptance, but a card should say 'experimental (gas phase)' rather than claim one type.

SO2 bondList has two S=O double bonds (expanded octet, formal charges all zero). Many general-chemistry texts draw one S=O and one S-O with +1/-1 formal charges as two resonance forms. Both give S +4 and a bent shape; spec 6.5 requires the app to state which it uses. This is an authored choice, not a data error.

H2O2: the CCCBDB H-O-O angle 94.8 is from 1962 and is 5 to 7.5 degrees below the later determinations in Herberth Table 5 (99.78 to 102.32). 94.8 is still the figure many textbooks print. Which set to show is the owner's decision; both coordinate sets verify.
NH3 106.67 and H2O 104.48 will display as 106.7 and 104.5; texts that print 107 or 107.3 for NH3 are quoting a different (ground-state) determination.
PubChem's title for CID 313 is 'Hydrochloric Acid'; the display name should stay 'Hydrogen chloride'.
